reconcile.note: Clarke reads the two swords as never meant for actual violence, keeping Luke's saying compatible with Jesus's rejection of the sword at his arrest.

discrepancy.note: Ernest Renan reads the sword episode naturalistically: Jesus weighs real self-defense, abandoning it only as impractical, not from principled non-resistance.

quotes.text: At one time Jesus thought of precautions and spoke of swords. There were two in the company. "It is enough," said he. He did not, however, follow out this idea; he saw clearly that timid provincials would not stand before the armed force of all the great powers of Jerusalem.
quotes.attr: Ernest Renan (1892), The Life of Jesus (1863), ch. 23.

sides.snippet: Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.
sides.verseText: Then Jesus said to him, \"Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.

sides.snippet: Whoever has none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.
sides.verseText: Then he said to them, \"But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a wallet. Whoever has none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.
